Jasper.java: Add simple chat loop
commitResults.messageBody:
To simulate a chatbot interaction, let's implement a simple chat loop
where commands entered by the user are echoed back until the user
exits with the command "bye".

commitResults.messageTitle: Jasper.java: Add list command to chat loop
commitResults.messageBody:
To keep track of user commands to process, let's add them to a list
instead of echoing them back and allow the user to view a numbered
list of their texts via the command "list".

Jasper.java: Add unmark command to mark tasks as undone
Consolidate task-level data and behaviour in a class Task
commitResults.messageBody:
Data related to a task (e.g. descriptor, completion status) are
stored separately, causing code duplication when parsing them.

Encapsulating these in a separate class also allows us to use
inheritance to extend and maintain new types of tasks later.

Let's put task-related data and behaviours (e.g. marking and unmarking
completion status) into a new class named Task.

Jasper.java: Refactor chat loop to use Tasks and switch expressions
commitResults.messageBody:
To leverage polymorphism, let's store different types of tasks as
instances of their parent Task class. Doing so will only expose
common functionality that the main chat loop needs to execute user
commands, reducing code duplication.

When parsing commands to execute, long and nested if statements make it
harder to read and maintain. Let's parse commands with switch
expressions instead to improves code quality with cleaner syntax that
is easier to reason about.

Jasper.java: Refactor command parsing and error handling
commitResults.messageBody:
Command parsing is verbose and handled completely by one function.

Separating parsing and error handling concerns is easier to extend
to manage more commands and more specific errors.

Let's delegate parsing a command's arguments, handling improper input
and execution to the class designed for each type of command.

Extract class TaskList.java to encapsulate operations on a Tasks list
commitResults.messageBody:
A raw list of tasks is passed around to multiple components.

This exposes its internal representation and violates Single
Responsibility Principle (SRP) by scattering repeated list operations
across the codebase.

Let's pull up behaviours by a list of Tasks into a new class
called TaskList.

This encapsulates list operations and reduces code duplication.
